memory_update.text: AMKR should be retained as the US-listed OSAT/reference capacity anchor for advanced packaging and test, but its market cap is now above the preferred small/mid-cap range; use it as context unless the exposure remains unusually pure.
CAMT is a high-priority underfollowed inspection/metrology candidate for AI advanced packaging, HBM, chiplets, hybrid bonding, and OSAT/HBM tool orders.

AEHR is a high-priority underfollowed test/burn-in candidate tied to AI processor wafer-level and package-level reliability screening, but customer concentration and order sustainability must be verified.

FORM, ONTO, PDFS, ACMR, COHU, TER, and substrate/material suppliers remain unscored coverage gaps for later Layer 1B passes focused on probe cards, inspection/metrology, yield analytics, test handlers, cleaning/plating, and substrates.

The advanced-packaging node should be decomposed into at least five subnodes for later validation: OSAT/foundry capacity, inspection/metrology, probe cards/test interface, burn-in/reliability, and substrates/materials.

node: Advanced packaging capacity, bonding, substrates, inspection, and test
summary: Layer 1B expanded the advanced-packaging bottleneck away from obvious GPU/foundry names into US-listed enablers of packaging throughput, inspection, and reliability qualification. TSMC/CoWoS remains the reference chokepoint, but the underfollowed research lane points to OSAT capacity, inspection/metrology for HBM and 2.5D/3D packages, and wafer/package-level burn-in for AI processors. This is research mapping only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
